render(<MyComponent />);\n145. \n146.     await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add Item' }));\n147. \n148.     // Assert on actual store state, not mock calls\n149.     await outside describe**: `const initialState = useMyStore.getState();`\n159. 2. **Reset in beforeEach AND afterEach**: Ensures test isolation\n160. 3. **Wrap setState in act()**: Required for React state When testing components that use Zustand stores, prefer **integration testing with real stores** over mocking.\n96. \n97. ### When to Use Real Stores vs Mocking\n98. \n99. **Use real stores (preferred)** when:\n100. \n101. - Testing components that modify store state\n102. - Verifying state changes after user interactions\n103. - Testing store action logic (merge, update, delete)\n104. \n105. **Mock the store** only when:\n106. \n107. - Testing pure UI components that only read from stores\n108. - Testing isolated component logic completely unrelated to state\n109. \n110. ### Pattern: Integration Testing with Real Stores\n111. \n112. **Reference**: `src/app/src/pages/redteam/setup/components/PluginsTab.test.tsx`\n113. \n114. ```typescript\n115. import { act, render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';\n116. import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';\n117. import { beforeEach, afterEach, describe, expect, test, vi } from 'vitest';\n118. import { useMyStore } from './useMyStore';\n119. \n120. // Capture initial state OUTSIDE describe block\n121. const initialState = useMyStore.getState();\n122. \n123. describe('MyComponent', () => {\n124.   beforeEach(() => {\n125.     // Reset store to initial state before each test\n126.     act(() => {\n127.       useMyStore.setState(initialState);\n128.     });\n129.   });\n130. \n131.   afterEach(() => {\n132.     // Clean up after each test\n133.     act(() => {\n134.       useMyStore.setState(initialState);\n135.     });\n136.   });\n137. \n138.   test('user interaction updates store correctly', async () => {\n139.     const user = userEvent.setup();\n140. \n141.     // Verify initial state\n142.     expect(useMyStore.getState().items).toHaveLength(0);\n143. \n144.     render(<MyComponent />);\n145. \n146.     await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add Item' }));\n147. \n148.     // Assert on actual store state, not mock calls\n149.     await waitFor(() => {\n150.       expect(useMyStore.getState().items).toHaveLength(1);\n151.     });\n152.   });\n153. });\n154. ```\n155. \n156. ### Key Patterns\n157. \n158. 1. **Capture initial state outside describe**: `const initialState = useMyStore.getState();`\n159. 2. **Reset in beforeEach AND afterEach**: Ensures test isolation\n160. 3. **Wrap setState in act()**: Required for React state batching\n161. 4. **Assert on getState()**: Verify actual store state, not that a mock was called\n162. 5. **Use waitFor for async**: Store updates may be asynchronous\n163. 6. **Mock external dependencies only**: Mock APIs, analytics, child components—NOT the store\n164. \n165. ### Anti-Pattern: Mocking the Store (avoid this)\n166. \n167. ```typescript\n168. // ❌ AVOID: Mocking the store hook loses integration coverage\n169. vi.mock('./useMyStore');\n170. const mockUpdateItems = vi.fn();\n171. (useMyStore as any).mockReturnValue({\n172.   items: [],\n173.   updateItems: mockUpdateItems,\n174. });\n175. \n176. test('clicking button calls updateItems', () => {\n177.   render(<MyComponent />);\n178.   fireEvent.click(button);\n179.   // Only verifies mock was called, not that store logic works\n180.   expect(mockUpdateItems).toHaveBeenCalled();\n181. });\n182. ```\n183. \n184. ### Additional Store Test References\n185. \n186. - `src/app/src/store/providersStore.test.ts` - Basic store testing\n187. - `src/app/src/stores/evalConfig.test.ts` - Configuration state\n188. - `src/app/src/stores/userStore.test.ts` - Async operations with act()\n189. \n190. ## Provider Testing\n191. \n192. They test `dist/src/main.js` directly using `spawnSync`.\n206. \n207. ```bash\n208. # Run smoke tests\n209. npm run test:smoke\n210. \n211. # Run specific smoke test file\n212. npx vitest run test/smoke/cli.test.ts --config vitest.smoke.config.ts\n213. ```\n214. \n215. **Location:** `test/smoke/` with fixtures in `test/smoke/fixtures/configs/`\n216. \n217. **Reference pattern** (from `test/smoke/filters-and-flags.test.ts`):\n218. \n219. ```typescript\n220. import { spawnSync } from 'child_process';\n221. import * as fs from 'fs';\n222. import * as path from 'path';\n223. import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';\n224. \n225. const CLI_PATH = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../dist/src/main.js');\n226. const FIXTURES_DIR = path.resolve(__dirname, 'fixtures/configs');\n227. const OUTPUT_DIR = path.resolve(__dirname, '.temp-output');\n228. \n229. function runCli(args: string[], options: { cwd?: string } = {}) {\n230.   const result = spawnSync('node', [CLI_PATH, ...args], {\n231.     cwd: options.cwd || path.resolve(__dirname, '../..'),\n232.     encoding: 'utf-8',\n233.     env: { ...process.env, NO_COLOR: '1' },\n234.     timeout: 60000,\n235.   });\n236.   return {\n237.     stdout: result.stdout || '',\n238.     stderr: result.stderr || '',\n239.     exitCode: result.status ?? 1,\n240.   };\n241. }\n242. \n243. describe('My Smoke Tests', () => {\n244.   beforeAll(() => {\n245.     if (!fs.existsSync(CLI_PATH)) {\n246.       throw new Error(`Built CLI not found. Run 'npm run build' first.`);\n247.     }\n248.     fs.mkdirSync(OUTPUT_DIR, { recursive: true });\n249.   });\n250. \n251.   afterAll(() => {\n252.     fs.rmSync(OUTPUT_DIR, { recursive: true, force: true });\n253.   });\n254. \n255.   it('runs eval with echo provider', () => {\n256.     const configPath = path.join(FIXTURES_DIR, 'basic.yaml');\n257.     const outputPath = path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, 'output.json');\n258. \n259.     const { exitCode } = runCli(['eval', '-c', configPath, '-o', outputPath, '--no-cache']);\n260. \n261.     expect(exitCode).toBe(0);\n262.     const parsed = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(outputPath, 'utf-8'));\n263.     expect(parsed.results.results[0].response.output).toContain('Hello');\n264.   });\n265. });\n266. ```\n267. \n268. **Key patterns:**\n269. \n270. - Test the **built package** (`dist/src/main.js`), not source code\n271. - Use `spawnSync` with `node` to run the CLI directly\n272. - Fixtures go in `test/smoke/fixtures/configs/` (committed to git)\n273. - Temp output directories cleaned up in `afterAll`\n274. - Use `echo` provider for deterministic, zero-cost testing\n275. - Check exit codes AND output file contents\n276. \n277. **Fixture example** (`test/smoke/fixtures/configs/basic.yaml`):\n278. \n279. ```yaml\n280. providers:\n281.   - echo\n282. \n283. prompts:\n284.   - 'Hello {{name}}'\n285. \n286. tests:\n287.   - vars:\n288.       name: World\n289.     assert:\n290.       - type: contains\n291.         value: World\n292. ```\n293. \n294. See `docs/plans/smoke-tests.md` for the full test checklist.\n295. \n296. ## Test Configuration\n297. \n298. - Config: `vitest.config.ts` (unit tests), `vitest.integration.config.ts` (integration tests), `vitest.smoke.config.ts` (smoke tests)\n299. - Setup: `vitest.setup.ts`\n300. - Globals disabled: All test utilities must be explicitly imported from `vitest`\n301. - Import `describe`, `it`, `expect`, `beforeEach`, `afterEach`, `vi` from `vitest`\n302. \n303. ## Testing Code with Timers\n304. \n305. When testing code that uses `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, or `Date.now()`, use **fake timers** to make tests deterministic and fast.\n306. \n307. **Reference files:**\n308. \n309. - `test/scheduler/slotQueue.test.ts` - Comprehensive fake timer usage\n310. - `test/scheduler/providerRateLimitState.test.ts` - Async code with timers\n311. \n312. ### Basic Pattern\n313. \n314. ```typescript\n315. import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';\n316. \n317. describe('MyTimerCode', () => {\n318.   beforeEach(() => {\n319.     vi.useFakeTimers();\n320.   });\n321. \n322.   afterEach(() => {\n323.     vi.useRealTimers();\n324.   });\n325. \n326.   it('handles timeout', () => {\n327.     const callback = vi.fn();\n328.     setTimeout(callback, 1000);\n329. \n330.     vi.advanceTimersByTime(1000);\n331. \n332.     expect(callback).toHaveBeenCalled();\n333.   });\n334. });\n335. ```\n336. \n337. ### Async Code with Timers\n338. \n339. When testing async functions that internally use timers, you cannot simply `await` them—the promise will hang because fake timers don't advance automatically. Use this pattern:\n340. \n341. ```typescript\n342. it('handles async retry with delay', async () => {\n343.   // 1. Start the promise (don't await yet)\n344.   const promise = myAsyncFunctionWithRetry();\n345. \n346.   // 2. Run all timers to completion\n347.   await vi.runAllTimersAsync();\n348. \n349.   // 3. Now await the result\n350.   const result = await promise;\n351. \n352.   expect(result).toBe('success');\n353. });\n354. ```\n355. \n356. ### Why Fake Timers Matter\n357. \n358. Real timers cause flaky tests because:\n359. \n360. - **Timer resolution varies**: Windows has ~15ms minimum resolution vs ~1-4ms on Linux/Mac\n361. - **Race conditions**: Code checking `Date.now()` multiple times can see different values if a millisecond boundary is crossed\n362. - **CI variability**: Tests may pass locally but fail under CI load\n363. \n364. **Anti-pattern** (causes flaky tests):\n365. \n366. ```typescript\n367. // ❌ AVOID: Real timers with small delays\n368. it('retries after delay', async () => {\n369.   const result = await functionThatRetries({ retryAfterMs: 1 }); // May timeout randomly\n370. });\n371. ```\n372. \n373. **Correct pattern**:\n374. \n375. ```typescript\n376. // ✓ CORRECT: Fake timers with controlled advancement\n377. it('retries after delay', async () => {\n378.   vi.useFakeTimers();\n379.   const promise = functionThatRetries({ retryAfterMs: 1000 });\n380.   await vi.runAllTimersAsync();\n381.   const result = await promise;\n382.   vi.useRealTimers();\n383. });\n384. ```\n385. \n386. ## Best Practices\n387. \n388. - Ensure all tests are independent and can run in any order\n389. - Clean up any test data or mocks after each test\n390. - Run the full test suite before committing changes\n391. - Test failures should be deterministic\n392. - For database tests, use in-memory instances or proper test fixtures\n393. - **Use fake timers** for any code involving `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, or timing-sensitive logic\n394.
